title: Test Join's website agent in browser
brief:
You are a usability tester for "Join", a web app where people get a group together (badminton, karaoke, escape room, board games, BBQ, hot pot...), negotiate the price with a venue, split it and pay with PayPal (sandbox only, no real money). You are playing a person who has NO AI agent of their own and uses the website's built-in agent.

The app runs on a machine on the local network: http://192.168.31.145:8799 . Do not restart, reconfigure or touch anything on that machine; just use the website.

Use the built-in browser tools (mcp__Claude_Browser__*; load them with ToolSearch if they are deferred). Open your OWN new tab (tabs_create, then navigate in that tab and pass its tabId) so you don't disturb other tabs. Sign in with this one-click demo link (no password involved):
http://192.168.31.145:8799/demo?as=hana&go=activity?agent=1
That opens the Activity page as "Hana Chen" with the agent drawer open (if closed, click "No agent? Ask Join's" bottom right). The drawer header says which model is used ("Qwen (qwen2.5:0.5b) on Join's own server").

What to do:
1. Hold at least 6 different conversations (use "New plan" between them), as a real person would type: mix Traditional Chinese and English, vague requests ("想跟朋友出去玩"), indirect ones ("something with singing", "想吃熱的鍋", "grill meat outside"), information spread over several messages, changing your mind mid-way (e.g. switching activity or day), typos, a budget given or not, naming friends (Alex, Ravi, Tomás, Yuki, Aisha, Leo, Noor, Sam, Ines, Kenji, Priya).
2. For at least two of them, pick an option ("Negotiate this") and go as far as the system allows: deal, the PayPal step (the sandbox may authorize automatically with a test card; if a PayPal button or sign-in page appears, DO NOT enter any credentials — just note it and stop there), or a refusal. Note how it handles being over budget / over Hana's limit and whether it offers alternatives.
3. Open the Activity page and "Plans" page afterwards and check that what the agent did is shown and matches what the drawer said.
4. Note anything confusing, wrong, misleading, inconsistent (e.g. language switching between Chinese and English, wrong dates/times — the town is in America/Los_Angeles time, wrong group size, misunderstood activity, numbers that don't add up), broken layout, errors, or slow responses.

Do not enter personal data, passwords or card numbers anywhere. Keep it under about 60 browser actions.

Final report (concise, plain text): for each conversation, what you typed (verbatim) and what the agent understood/did; then a numbered list of problems, each with exact steps to reproduce, what you expected and what happened, and a severity (high/medium/low). Separate facts you saw from your opinions.

Everything below is what I saw, except where marked "Opinion". Each drawer reply took about 10 seconds or less, and I saw no errors or broken layout. The Activity and Plans pages matched what the drawer said on all numbers and dates. The drawer header said "Qwen (qwen2.5:0.5b) on Join's own server". The drawer was open the whole time, and I stayed on the Activity page except when checking Plans.

**Conversations**

1. Karaoke, indirect and spread over messages.
   - I typed "想跟朋友出去玩". It replied in Chinese asking what I wanted to do.
   - I typed "something with singing, me Alex and Ravi". It asked which day, in English.
   - I typed "saturday night, budget $20 each". It said "Looking for karaoke for 3, about $20 each…" and showed 3 options, all Echo Karaoke at 18:00, 20:00 and 22:00. Each was $36.00 ($12.00 each) for Hana, Alex and Tomás.
   - Ravi, whom I named, was replaced by Tomás without comment.
